newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia appeals to EU for earthquake help.
newsitem.headline: Croatia appeals to EU for earthquake help.

text.p: Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic asked the European Union (EU) on Monday for urgent help for an area on the Adriatic coast which was badly damaged in an earthquake last week, the Croatian news agency HINA reported.
HINA also said an aftershock hit the area around the town of Ston on Monday, the biggest tremor since Thursday's quake, triggering landslides which closed the main coastal road.

Granic made his appeal in a letter to European Commissioner Hans van den Broek, who is responsible for post-communist Europe, and Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring. Ireland holds the rotating EU presidency.
Granic said last Thursday's earthquake around Ston had undone all work to repair severe damage suffered in the Croatian-Serb war of 1991.
HINA did not say what kind of help he had requested.
The population of Ston was evacuated after the tremor measuring 6.0 on the Richter scale, in which one person was reported slightly injured.
Monday's aftershock at 5.57 pm (1557 GMT) measured 5.4, according to the Zagreb Institute of Seismology.
